metadata.name: NASA Ames B0005 Battery Aging Dataset
metadata.provenance: NASA Ames Prognostics Center of Excellence (PCoE)

poisson.adequacy_rationale: Dispersion index D = 8.63 significantly exceeds 1.0. Event variance exceeds the Poisson mean, indicating event clustering or non-stationary aging.
limitations: Assumes constant event rate λ throughout the entire cycle series.
Assumes independence between discharge cycles (no memory or degradation carryover).
Sensitive to temporal clustering during battery end-of-life knee points.

exponential.adequacy_rationale: Observed CV = 2.54 significantly exceeds 1.0. Inter-event waiting times exhibit heavy-tailed or clustered clustering, violating memoryless Exponential arrivals.
limitations: Assumes a memoryless process: probability of an event in the next window is independent of elapsed time.
Assumes constant hazard rate throughout the observation lifecycle.
Truncation and right-censoring at observation window endpoints can bias empirical intervals.

shift_evidence: Non-overlapping 95% Garwood confidence intervals between Early-Life (Pristine) [0.124, 0.4192] and Late-Life (Knee Point / Aging) [15.4714, 17.5612].
Late-stage event rate is 68.7x higher than early-stage baseline.
regime_shift.recommendation: The constant-rate assumption (homogeneous Poisson process) is violated across the battery lifespan. Predictive safety systems must employ piecewise or degradation-indexed rates rather than a single global λ.
regime_shift.caveat: Correlation between thermal events and discharge cycle index reflects electrochemical degradation; causation should not be inferred without multi-physics cell impedance characterization.

threshold_sensitivity.narrative: Varying the threshold from 36.0°C to 45.0°C reduces total observed events by 12262 (12262 down to 0), shifting estimated cycle event rate λ from 72.988 to 0.000. This sensitivity demonstrates how engineering threshold selection directly drives downstream risk probabilities.
threshold_sensitivity.disclaimer: Thresholds evaluated in this studio represent analytical research scenarios. They do not constitute certified OEM limits or physical failure boundaries.

decision_center.disclaimer: ThermoScope is an analytical research and decision-support application. Its thresholds and alert rules are not certified safety limits. It does not independently predict or prevent thermal runaway and does not replace a certified battery management system or manufacturer safety procedures.
